key_insight: General-purpose LLMs outperform domain-specific pretrained models in the reported alloy-property benchmarks, with further gains from numerical predictions supplied as prompts.
engineering_relevance: Combining existing property predictors with general-purpose LLMs could improve alloy screening accuracy while reducing reliance on costly domain-specific pretraining.
method: Benchmark general-purpose LLMs against SteelBERT, MatSciBERT, and SciBERT on Ti, steel, high-entropy alloy, and Al datasets.
Prompt DeepSeek V3.1 and Gemini-2.5-Flash with CatBoost or SteelBERT predictions to guide corrections.
Evaluate similarity-based reference-data selection and self-reported prediction confidence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that using only 5% of high-similarity training references achieves performance similar to using the full training set, while high self-reported confidence correlates with smaller prediction errors.
watch_item: Validate performance and confidence calibration on independently held-out, distribution-shifted alloys before relying on predictions for engineering decisions.
paper_title: Quantifying out-of-distribution data severity with Wasserstein distances: benchmarking large language models for alloy property prediction
